nodes.label: ADR-0001: Presentation over coverage
nodes.rationale: The tool definitions cost about 18,900 tokens per turn. Full ADT coverage (~350 tools, from 215 discovery collections) would cost about 51,000. The smallest client in scope (an 8B model with a 128k window) is the design target, and reliability there came from better tools, not more of them. The tool counts disagree across documents: this ADR's title says 139 and its body 138, while Tool-Reference lists 128.

nodes.norm_label: adr-0002: composite tools where the protocol is the hard part
nodes.rationale: The four-step edit cycle's ordering, the lifetime of the lock handle and the obligation to unlock after a failure were all outside the schemas, written as prose. A rule a model has to remember across four calls is one it will sometimes forget, and an orphaned lock on a shared system blocks other developers. The demand for the composite was explicit, which meets ADR-0001's evidence bar.

nodes.norm_label: up-front batch validation, per-member execution errors

nodes.label: Design decision: one code path for one or many RFC calls (runCalls / invokeJsonRpcBatch)
nodes.norm_label: design decision: one code path for one or many rfc calls (runcalls / invokejsonrpcbatch)
nodes.rationale: Everything above the transport is count-agnostic. Only the wire format branches (object vs array), because the SAP processor branches on it. That leaves the single-call behaviour verified on DEV/100 untouched.

nodes.label: SRFC package node as cheap RFC-callability check
nodes.norm_label: srfc package node as cheap rfc-callability check
nodes.rationale: RFC_GET_FUNCTION_INTERFACE reads any function module's signature, RFC-enabled or not, so a successful readAbapFunctionModule is documentation, not proof the module is callable. The SRFC node lists the RFC-enabled modules without calling one.

nodes.label: Client system-prompt rules (prefer by-name tools, constrain SELECTs)
nodes.norm_label: client system-prompt rules (prefer by-name tools, constrain selects)
nodes.rationale: Fall back to searchObject -> objectStructure -> getObjectSource only when intermediate results are needed and never hand-craft /sap/bc/adt paths; SAP tables are large, so always constrain SELECTs with WHERE, SELECT SINGLE or UP TO n ROWS. SAP is decoupled from the local file system.

nodes.label: Tag every claim with its evidence source
nodes.norm_label: tag every claim with its evidence source
nodes.rationale: Each claim rests on SMODILOG, a marker block with its transport, or a version-database diff. An assertion that fits none of the three is an inference and must be marked as one.

nodes.label: State where each finding came from
nodes.norm_label: state where each finding came from
nodes.rationale: System findings (an ATC priority, a syntax error) are facts, while a style remark is a judgement. A reviewer weighs the two differently, so they must not be presented in the same voice.

nodes.label: Step 0: prefer the system's own checks when ADT is available
nodes.norm_label: step 0: prefer the system's own checks when adt is available
nodes.rationale: The system's syntax check and ATC are authoritative: they know the DDIC, the release and what will actually activate. Do not ask the user to paste code you can read yourself.

nodes.label: Avoid Obsolete Language Elements
nodes.rationale: Newer alternatives improve readability, keep benefitting from optimizations, and ease onboarding of young ABAPers.

nodes.label: Write Comments to Explain the Why, Not the What
nodes.norm_label: write comments to explain the why, not the what

nodes.label: Use Constants Instead of Magic Numbers
nodes.norm_label: use constants instead of magic numbers

nodes.label: CL_ABAP_GARBAGE_COLLECTOR
nodes.rationale: The ABAP runtime invokes the garbage collector periodically, so a manual collect() is only worth it in exceptional cases such as large unneeded objects, resource-constrained environments, or memory analysis.

nodes.label: Runtime Types, UUIDs and System Information
nodes.norm_label: runtime types, uuids and system information

nodes.label: sy components usable in ABAP for Cloud Development
nodes.norm_label: sy components usable in abap for cloud development
nodes.rationale: Only selected sy fields (index, tabix, dbcnt, subrc, langu, uname, msg*) are usable in ABAP Cloud; others such as sy-datum should not be used, and XCO_CP offers XCO representations instead.

nodes.label: PCRE preferred over obsolete POSIX REGEX
nodes.norm_label: pcre preferred over obsolete posix regex
nodes.rationale: The REGEX addition with POSIX syntax is obsolete and raises a syntax warning (suppressible via ##REGEX_POSIX); use CREATE_PCRE or the PCRE addition instead.

nodes.label: Test doubles replace dependent-on components (DOC)
nodes.rationale: Standardized test double frameworks replace dependent-on components (classes, database tables/CDS entities, RAP BOs) during unit tests so logic can be tested in isolation.

nodes.label: ADT discovery capability gate
nodes.rationale: Every failure path leaves the gate empty and the list complete: hiding a tool that would have worked is worse than offering one that errors, because the first is invisible.

nodes.label: Coverage
nodes.rationale: Measured against the system's own discovery document; a diagnostic, not a target.

nodes.label: ABAP_MCP_GATE startup capability check
nodes.rationale: Asks the system what it supports and withholds tools whose ADT collections are absent (10 abapGit and 3 service-binding tools on DEV) that would otherwise answer HTTP 400; one discovery round trip per process, can only shorten the list, any failure leaves every tool listed.

nodes.label: healthcheck tool
nodes.rationale: Sits outside every profile because it is the tool that answers which profile is running; reports profile, responseBudgetBytes, withheld tools and system identity.

nodes.label: One server entry per system/client (SAP_SYSTEM_ID)
nodes.rationale: A server is bound to one system and client for its whole life; announcing SAP_SYSTEM_ID in the MCP instructions lets an agent route a request to the right server without calling anything.

nodes.label: Declared vs observed system identity check
nodes.norm_label: declared vs observed system identity check
nodes.rationale: SAP names system and client in the session cookie (SAP_SESSIONID_DEV_100); a mismatch with SAP_SYSTEM_ID raises a healthcheck WARNING because every tool would otherwise keep working, just on the wrong system.

nodes.label: Locks Held in Stateful Session (dropSession Escape Hatch)
nodes.norm_label: locks held in stateful session (dropsession escape hatch)

nodes.label: Basis Skill (Running System Inspection)
nodes.rationale: Answers operational questions about what a running system is doing from an ADT session rather than SAP GUI; repository questions belong to the abap / clean-abap skills.

nodes.label: Logged-on Users Are Per Application Server (TH_USER_LIST / SM04)
nodes.norm_label: logged-on users are per application server (th_user_list / sm04)
nodes.rationale: TH_USER_LIST reports only the instance the session is connected to (SM04, not AL08); on a multi-instance system 'nobody logged on' means nobody on this instance, so answers must say so.

nodes.label: logonType / logonState / logonProtocol Kept as Raw Integers
nodes.norm_label: logontype / logonstate / logonprotocol kept as raw integers
nodes.rationale: Data elements UEXT_TYPE, USTATE and UPROTOCOL have no domain, so any label would be invented; observable fields (transaction, guiVersion, rfcType) are used instead.

nodes.label: Separate Service Users from Named Users
nodes.norm_label: separate service users from named users
nodes.rationale: Most sessions belong to technical users (SAPJSF_*, BGRFCSUPER, SAPSYS, RFC*) and the MCP server's own HTTP/ICF session appears too, so raw counts overstate human usage; a filtered zero must quote filter.totalBeforeFilter.

nodes.label: RAP Locking and ETag Concurrency Control
nodes.norm_label: rap locking and etag concurrency control

nodes.label: Application Log, Locking and Number Ranges Reference
nodes.norm_label: application log, locking and number ranges reference

nodes.label: Do not use sy-datum/sy-uzeit in ABAP for Cloud Development
nodes.norm_label: do not use sy-datum/sy-uzeit in abap for cloud development
nodes.rationale: Date and time system fields are not to be used in ABAP Cloud; user-related date/time values come from the XCO library or CL_ABAP_CONTEXT_INFO instead.

nodes.label: Component Allowlist Discipline
nodes.rationale: Do not add familiar products as decoration; preserve the requested sequence as an ordered edge list without inserting intermediaries.

nodes.label: IF_BGMC_OP_SINGLE
nodes.rationale: Used with transactional control (e.g. RAP); in a RAP context COMMIT/ROLLBACK WORK is not needed because the RAP framework takes care of it.

nodes.label: Controlled SAP LUW
nodes.rationale: Database modifications are only allowed in the save transactional phase because data processed in the modify phase may be inconsistent and could disrupt the SAP LUW.

nodes.label: Never write to stdout convention
nodes.rationale: The server speaks MCP over stdio; anything on stdout that is not a protocol frame corrupts the stream. This has broken every tool at once before.

nodes.label: Logger wrote info/debug to stdout (fixed bug)
nodes.norm_label: logger wrote info/debug to stdout (fixed bug)

nodes.label: RAP OData UI service with Fiori Elements preview for XLSX upload
nodes.norm_label: rap odata ui service with fiori elements preview for xlsx upload
nodes.rationale: Generated only to get XLSX content into the system as an xstring to work with; it is not related to the XCO library itself.

nodes.label: XLSX row stream and cursor access
nodes.norm_label: xlsx row stream and cursor access

nodes.label: Security considerations when importing external XLSX content
nodes.norm_label: security considerations when importing external xlsx content
nodes.rationale: The example is for demonstration only; importing and processing external content needs the security precautions from the XCO XLSX read-access documentation.

nodes.label: Response budget ceiling
nodes.rationale: serializeResult() is the single funnel every answer passes through, so the ceiling covers new tools automatically; over-budget answers become valid JSON stating size and next step rather than a cut-off fragment a model would retry.

nodes.label: First-try success
nodes.rationale: The measure of quality; tool count and token cost matter only through their effect on it.

nodes.label: editAbapSource tool
nodes.rationale: core is small because this one tool is the whole write cycle (lock, write, unlock, activate), releasing the lock even when a step fails.

nodes.label: ABAP_MCP_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES response ceiling
nodes.rationale: The tool list is a fixed cost but an answer is unbounded; an over-budget answer is withheld and replaced by valid JSON (status:truncated, bytes, budget, preview, nextStep), never a cut-off fragment that would not parse and would invite the identical retry.

nodes.label: ABAP_MCP_PROFILE tool profiles (core/analyst/rfc/dev/all)
nodes.rationale: A client that cannot fetch tool schemas on demand pays for the whole tool list every turn (core ~2,737 tokens vs all ~17,759). A profile is not a convenience filter: out-of-profile tools are neither listed nor routed, so analyst guarantees nothing edits source; an unrecognised profile name stops the server instead of silently serving 129 tools.

nodes.label: Wrap foreign exceptions instead of letting them invade your code
nodes.norm_label: wrap foreign exceptions instead of letting them invade your code

nodes.label: JSON-RPC Batch Shares One LUW (Rollback Probe)
nodes.norm_label: json-rpc batch shares one luw (rollback probe)
nodes.rationale: State-changing calls are operational actions needing user confirmation; ending a batch with BAPI_TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK is the safe way to probe a write.

nodes.label: A readable signature is not a callable function module
nodes.norm_label: a readable signature is not a callable function module

nodes.label: Avoid Encodings, Hungarian Notation and Prefixes
nodes.norm_label: avoid encodings, hungarian notation and prefixes
nodes.rationale: Encoding prefixes (iv_, rv_, lt_) make names needlessly longer; may be better ignored in legacy projects to avoid a breach between old and new code.

nodes.label: Boy Scout Rule
nodes.rationale: Always leave edited code a little cleaner than you found it; small extra minutes accumulate over time.

nodes.label: Clean Islands
nodes.rationale: Fully cleaned small components demonstrate the benefit and form tested home bases for further refactoring.

nodes.label: Four-Step Legacy Refactoring Plan
nodes.rationale: Get the team aboard, follow the boy scout rule, build clean islands, talk about it - gradual adoption avoids disputes and accumulates improvements.

nodes.label: Kerberos / SPNEGO SSO mode
nodes.rationale: Node cannot do SPNEGO, so the server shells out to curl --negotiate.

nodes.label: healthcheck tool (profile, system identity, reachability layers)
nodes.norm_label: healthcheck tool (profile, system identity, reachability layers)

nodes.label: JSON-RPC protocol facts (/IWBEP/CL_JSRPC_*)
nodes.rationale: Unmatched or lower-case parameter keys are dropped silently. Calls therefore go through callFunctionViaJsonRpc, which upper-cases the keys and validates them against the real signature.

nodes.label: Response and error model (single-level MCP envelope, handleError)
nodes.norm_label: response and error model (single-level mcp envelope, handleerror)

nodes.label: SSO session bootstrap and injection (bootstrapSsoSession / injectSsoSession)
nodes.norm_label: sso session bootstrap and injection (bootstrapssosession / injectssosession)
nodes.rationale: Kerberos shells out to curl --negotiate because Node cannot do SPNEGO. Injecting the SAP_SESSIONID cookies and the CSRF token flips AdtHTTP to logged-in, so it never Basic-auths with the placeholder.

nodes.label: Offline test suites (handlerContract, toolDefinitions, jsonRpcHandlers, ...)
nodes.rationale: The suites run against fakes of ADTClient, so they prove the wrapper contract (argument mapping, envelopes, error translation), not how any ADT endpoint behaves.

nodes.label: ToolDefinition contract (inputSchema, narrowingHint, needsFeature)
nodes.rationale: There is no optional:true flag because it was never JSON Schema; required is the only optionality marker. Arguments are still not schema-validated at the door, so handlers validate what they can.

nodes.label: SSO bootstrap via curl --negotiate (SSO_CURL_PATH)
nodes.rationale: Shells out to the Windows System32 curl.exe because it needs curl's Schannel/SSPI backend; other platforms must point SSO_CURL_PATH at a curl built with GSS-API.

nodes.label: ABAP ADT MCP Server - Complete Tool Reference (MCP-Tools.md)
nodes.norm_label: abap adt mcp server - complete tool reference (mcp-tools.md)

nodes.label: Tool annotations convention (title + four hints)
nodes.rationale: OpenAI's directory rejects a tool that omits destructiveHint/idempotentHint, and omitted hints make clients fall back to not-read-only, destructive, open-world defaults.

nodes.label: Authentication modes (Kerberos, X.509, OAuth, password - never Basic with placeholder)
nodes.norm_label: authentication modes (kerberos, x.509, oauth, password - never basic with placeholder)
nodes.rationale: The heuristics prefer credentials that cannot lock a SAP user. The placeholder password is never sent, so Basic attempts cannot lock a technical user. The credential is presented once and the session cookie carries the rest, so a short-lived OAuth token is not a problem.

nodes.label: One-LUW batch for an update BAPI and its commit
nodes.norm_label: one-luw batch for an update bapi and its commit
nodes.rationale: The members of a JSON-RPC array request run in one ABAP session and roll area. Separate calls land in different LUWs, so the BAPI's changes are lost. Verified live with an insert, a read-back and a rollback in one batch.

nodes.label: Request lifecycle and routing table derived from getTools()
nodes.norm_label: request lifecycle and routing table derived from gettools()
nodes.rationale: Deriving the routing table from getTools() means a tool cannot be listed without being callable. Duplicate names are refused at startup, and TOOL_ALIASES keeps renamed tools callable without listing them.

nodes.label: Per-profile response size ceiling (status:truncated)
nodes.rationale: An over-budget answer comes back as valid JSON with a 2,000-byte preview and a nextStep instead of a cut-off fragment. Retrying the identical call gives the identical refusal, so the caller has to narrow the request with a filter, a name or a row limit.

nodes.label: Never log to stdout - stderr-only logger
nodes.norm_label: never log to stdout - stderr-only logger
nodes.rationale: The server speaks MCP over stdio, so a stray console.log in a handler corrupts the protocol stream for every tool.

nodes.label: System identity binding (SAP_SYSTEM_ID declared vs observed)
nodes.norm_label: system identity binding (sap_system_id declared vs observed)
nodes.rationale: There is one server per system and client. The id observed in the session cookie beats the declared one. A mismatch warns rather than refusing to start, because the damage comes from routing, not execution, and failing hard would brick a server after a system copy or rename.

nodes.label: MCP tool annotations (readOnly / destructive / idempotent / openWorld hints)
nodes.norm_label: mcp tool annotations (readonly / destructive / idempotent / openworld hints)
nodes.rationale: The hints let a client auto-approve the 82 read-only tools and prompt on the rest. They are not a permission system. Each tool declares them next to its name, so a rename cannot silently drop them. All four flags are always stated because OpenAI's tool directory rejects omissions, and client defaults would read a missing destructiveHint as true.

nodes.label: Two-layer reachability probe (/sap/public/ping + /sap/bc/ping)
nodes.rationale: SAP answers 403 before offering a logon, so an 'icf' layer failure must not be read as an authentication failure.

nodes.label: diagnosing-bugs skill
nodes.rationale: Fits the class of bug this project produces, where the failure is in SAP's behaviour rather than in the TypeScript.

nodes.label: A status code is not a diagnosis
nodes.norm_label: a status code is not a diagnosis
nodes.rationale: 401 and 403 mean different layers; conflating them reported an inactive ADT ICF node as a missing Kerberos ticket on two systems for two days.

nodes.label: Prefer Functional to Procedural Language Constructs
nodes.norm_label: prefer functional to procedural language constructs

nodes.label: Prefer LINE_EXISTS to READ TABLE or LOOP AT
nodes.norm_label: prefer line_exists to read table or loop at
